decision_basis: Qualitative project choice prioritizing the observed improvement in non-IID attack protection while retaining honest-stripe accuracy above RFA. It is not a scalar optimum or a claim that one method wins every condition.
rationale: Compared with v0.5, non-IID persistent label-flip damage decreased in all five blocks and absolute attacked accuracy increased in all five blocks.
Compared with RFA, v0.6 retained higher mean honest-stripe accuracy in both regimes.
The final implementation uses zero server reference images and one unchanged rule in IID and non-IID.
reporting_rules: Use the same matched blocks for every numerical comparison.
Report clean-relative damage alongside absolute attacked accuracy.
Use the same v0.6 algorithm for both regimes; do not combine v0.5 IID results and v0.6 non-IID results as one method.
Retain all failed gates and earlier pilot outcomes.
Existing v0.3 component controls do not become v0.6 ablations or recovery evidence.
Distinguish literature-inspired engineering choices and measured usefulness from an established originality claim.
role: Primary proposed method in the project report and demonstration; remains an evaluated experimental prototype.
selection_history: Outcome-informed choice after development and five-block follow-up. All five original block conditions had informed development; these are not untouched confirmatory results.
supported_conclusion: In this controlled MNIST workload, adding per-client innovation clipping to v0.5 reduced non-IID poisoning damage and attack-onset vulnerability, with a measurable IID stripe-adaptation cost. RFA retained better mean attack protection; v0.6 retained better honest-stripe accuracy.
tradeoffs: IID stripe accuracy was lower than v0.5 in four of five blocks; its mean loss was1.1176 percentage points.
Non-IID clean, noise and absolute attacked accuracy remained lower than RFA on average.
The mean non-IID honest-stripe gain over v0.5 was0.5014 points, but its paired interval crosses zero; it is not an established general improvement.
v0.6 adds per-client vector history and can delay legitimate adaptation or retain poisoned history.
uncertainty: Five paired development blocks; report block values and nominal two-sided95% t intervals(df4). Assumes independent approximately normal block differences, unstable at n=5, no simultaneous coverage and no independent-confirmation claim.
unsupported_claims: Proof that an unusual client update is malicious
Established novelty or inherited theoretical guarantees from the motivating literature
General concept-drift handling beyond the tested input interventions
Attack-stop recovery, recurring attacks, mixed events or adaptive attacks for v0.6
Secure aggregation, differential privacy, Sybil resistance or malicious-count protection

v06_coverage.evaluation: Development legitimate-task evaluation; no official test set used.
